teaser.text: China Hongqiao Group Limited is an industrial aluminum maker: it turns ore, electricity and processing capacity into metal and components for other businesses. To understand how money comes in and goes out, follow the chain from bauxite to customer, then follow the cash through costs, customers and investment.

stock.title: Hongqiao stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Hongqiao’s forecast weighs scenario prices against durable margins, free cash flow and valuation.
stock.opening: The weighted share-price outcome is HKD17.81 by October 2027 and HKD15.20 by October 2029. It hinges on durable margins and cash covering investment, dividends, debt and Simandou funding calls.
stock.closing: The full memo also covers Hongqiao’s business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast offers modest positive total returns, but not a convincing share-price rerating. The weighted share-price outcome is HKD17.81 by October 2027, HKD16.09 by October 2028 and HKD15.20 by October 2029, against HKD19.64 today.

By October 2029, the modeled outcomes run from HKD13.59 in the bull case to HKD18.87 in the bear case. That counterintuitive ordering reflects the bull case's heavier dilution and investment spending, which prevent stronger operations from translating into a higher equity value. The bear, base and bull probabilities are 28%, 50% and 22%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Hongqiao?

paragraphs.text: The base case therefore chooses RMB30,000 million, RMB28,000 million and RMB29,000 million across the three dates. The bear path falls to RMB24,000 million, RMB15,000 million and RMB18,000 million as aluminum prices weaken and input costs rise. The bull path reaches RMB39,000 million, RMB42,000 million and RMB45,000 million through Yunnan power, Indonesian capacity and deeper processing. Deep-processed volume rose 23.2% in H1 2026, but alumina margin fell to 6.3%, so both paths remain credible.

The bear case requires a cyclical margin reversal while Hongqiao continues funding investment. Aluminum prices fall, alumina costs recover and weaker earnings persist into 2028–29. Net debt reaches RMB41,605 million by 2029 as projects, dividends and working-capital demands absorb cash. The shares reach HKD18.78 in 2027 and HKD18.87 in 2029, with a 28% probability. That is material because operating profit previously fell to RMB11,379 million and alumina margin has already weakened.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Hongqiao really make?

paragraphs.text: The five-year record shows revenue and earnings recovering after a cash-flow downturn. The company’s free cash flow, computed from its cash-flow statement as cash from operations minus capital spending, lease payments and interest paid, turned negative in 2022; diluted EPS recovered, but cash per share remains the sharper test after investment. Buybacks returned cash at a 3.1% yield alongside an 8.4% dividend yield.

dividend.title: Hongqiao dividend
dividend.meta_description: Hongqiao's dividend varies with earnings and cash flow; investment, debt and project funding can constrain payouts.
dividend.opening: Hongqiao's forecast dividend per share ranges from CNY0.50 to CNY2.90, with a base path of CNY2.10, CNY1.90 and CNY1.80. Hongqiao's cash coverage is cyclical: free cash flow turned negative in 2022, and future funding needs could constrain dividends or buybacks.
dividend.closing: The full Hongqiao memo also answers questions about its business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: What dividend does Hongqiao pay over time?

paragraphs.text: Dividends follow earnings but normalize as investment continues. The base case selects CNY2.10, CNY1.90 and CNY1.80 per share, supported initially by the CNY3.49983 analyst EPS estimate but reduced after H1 2026 produced no interim dividend. The bear case cuts DPS from CNY1.40 to CNY0.70 and CNY0.50 as cash tightens; the bull case rises from CNY2.30 to CNY2.60 and CNY2.90. The range reflects dividends falling sharply during the last downturn and negative free cash flow in 2022.

blocks.heading: Is Hongqiao's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is the operating cash left after investment spending. It can fund dividends and buybacks, but those payments do not create operating cash. Hongqiao’s five-year record shows strong cash generation in some years and negative free cash flow in another, so a large payout in a strong year may not be sustainable.
